pages.title: deployment
pages.description: LangSmith Deployment is framework-agnostic which means you can deploy agents built with:

pages.title: deployment-quickstart
pages.description: This quickstart shows you how to deploy an application to LangSmith Cloud in GCP using the [`langgraph deploy`](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/cli#deploy) command. Any app that exports a graph from a [`langgraph.json`](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/application-structure#configuration-file-concepts) config deploys the same way, regardless of which framework you used to author the agent.

pages.title: deployment-revisions
pages.description: A revision deploys a version of your application to an existing Cloud deployment. Create a revision to release code changes without creating another deployment.

pages.title: evaluation
pages.description: LangSmith's testing tools help you measure agent quality, iterate on prompts, and debug live in an interactive environment. Evaluation is the core of testing: it scores your agent's outputs against datasets and criteria so you can benchmark versions, catch regressions, and track quality over time.

pages.title: evaluation-approaches
pages.description: Below, we will discuss evaluation of a few popular types of LLM applications.

pages.title: evaluation-async
pages.description: We can run evaluations asynchronously via the SDK using [aevaluate()](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langsmith/evaluation/_arunner/aevaluate), which accepts all of the same arguments as [evaluate()](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langsmith/evaluation/_runner/evaluate) but expects the application function to be asynchronous. To learn more, see [how to use the `evaluate()` function](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-llm-application).

pages.title: evaluation-concepts
pages.description: LLM outputs are non-deterministic, which makes response quality hard to assess. Evaluations (evals) are a way to breakdown what "good" looks like and measure it. LangSmith Evaluation provides a framework for measuring quality throughout the application lifecycle, from pre-deployment testing to production monitoring.

pages.title: evaluation-quickstart
pages.description: Running an evaluation in LangSmith requires three key components:

pages.title: evaluation-types
pages.description: This page covers two aspects of evaluation in LangSmith:

pages.title: fleet
pages.description: LangSmith Fleet is a no-code platform for creating and managing AI agents. It allows you to create agents from templates, connect your accounts, and let the agent handle routine work while you stay in control.

pages.title: access-and-oversight
pages.description: Fleet gives you the control layer for scaling agents across your organization: tiered permissions, credential management, human-in-the-loop oversight, and an audit trail for agent actions.

pages.title: agent-identity
pages.description: Agent identity controls whose [credentials](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/workspace-admin.md) the agent uses when it interacts with apps and services.

pages.title: arcade
pages.description: When you connect Arcade to your workspace, a workspace admin selects an Arcade organization and project, then installs MCP gateways from that project. Each user connects their own Arcade account so that tool calls authenticate with their individual credentials.

pages.title: auth-format
pages.description: Some [tools](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/tools.md) require user authorization (for example, Google, Slack, GitHub). LangSmith Fleet includes middleware to detect when a tool needs authorization and to pause the run with a clear prompt to the user. After the user completes auth, the same tool call is retried automatically.

pages.title: changelog
pages.description: Weekly updates to [LangSmith Fleet](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet.md).

pages.title: channels
pages.description: Channels define when your agent starts running. Connect your agent to external events so it responds automatically to messages, emails, or other events.

pages.title: code
pages.description: There are two main ways to use Fleet agents programmatically:

pages.title: comparison
pages.description: Of the platforms compared here, only Fleet works with any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible API endpoint regardless of cloud provider.

pages.title: computer-use
pages.description: Computer use gives your Fleet agent access to an isolated virtual computer. The agent can write and execute code, manage files, install packages, and call authenticated external APIs without exposing credentials to the language model.

pages.title: essentials
pages.description: LangSmith Fleet essentials are the core features that make up the foundation of your agents. They include tools, channels, memory, sub-agents, and approvals.

pages.title: No-code agents with LangSmith Fleet
pages.description: Create helpful AI agents without code. Start from a template, connect your accounts, and let the agent handle routine work while you stay in control

pages.title: manage-agent-settings
pages.description: This page explains how to manage the settings for your agents in LangSmith Fleet.

pages.title: mcp-framework
pages.description: The LangSmith Tool Server is a standalone MCP framework for building and deploying tools with built-in authentication and authorization. Use the Tool Server when you want to:

pages.title: quickstart
pages.description: By the end of this quickstart, you will have an Executive Assistant that labels the Gmail messages needing your attention and pauses for approval before acting, all set up without code or a model API key and controlled through chat.

pages.title: remote-mcp-servers
pages.description: You can connect LangSmith Fleet to remote MCP servers to extend your agents with additional tools and integrations. This page covers how to add custom MCP servers and provides configuration details for popular remote servers.

pages.title: salesforce
pages.description: The Salesforce integration gives your agents read-only access to data in your Salesforce org. Once connected, an agent can:

pages.title: schedules
pages.description: Schedules run your agent on a recurring time-based schedule. Use schedules when your agent needs to do work proactively, not just in response to a message or event.

pages.title: skills
pages.description: Skills are reusable capabilities that provide specialized workflows and domain knowledge to your agent. Each skill is stored in the agent's long-term memory at `memories/skills/<skill-name>`. The skill's name and description is loaded when the agent starts. Based on this info the agent can decide to use the skill. The full skill file is only loaded when the agent determines it is relevant to the current task. Any referenced additional resources may be loaded by the agent if they become relevant.

pages.title: slack-app
pages.description: Fleet turns any agent into a Slack teammate your team can tag in a channel or message directly. The bot is the agent, not a relay in front of it: it runs with the agent's own instructions, tools, and permissions. Every agent can have its own Slack app, so a single Slack workspace can run as many Slack bots as you have agents: one triaging support, one watching the on-call rotation, one digging through research.

pages.title: teams-app
pages.description: With LangSmith Fleet, you can connect your agents to Microsoft Teams by registering a custom Azure Bot. Once connected, your agents can:

pages.title: templates
pages.description: LangSmith Fleet includes [starter templates](https://www.langchain.com/templates) to help you create agents quickly. Templates include predefined instructions, [tools](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/tools.md), and [channels](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/essentials.md#channels) (if applicable) for common use cases. You can use templates as-is, or as a baseline to customize.

pages.title: tools
pages.description: You can access a variety of tools in LangSmith Fleet. Use tool integrations and [MCP servers](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/fleet/remote-mcp-servers.md) to give your agents access to email, calendars, chat, project management, code hosting, spreadsheets/BI, search, social, and general web utilities.

pages.title: webhooks
pages.description: When triggered, a webhook sends a complete package of your agent's configuration and files to the specified endpoint.

pages.title: workspace-admin
pages.description: Configure workspace secrets and manage spend limits for Fleet agents and users.

pages.title: manage-contexts-sdk
pages.description: Use the LangSmith [Python](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smith-python-sdk.md) and [TypeScript](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/smith-js-ts-sdk.md) SDKs to manage **agent repos** and **skill repos** in the [Context Hub](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-the-context-hub.md) programmatically. [Push](#push-an-agent) new versions from CI, [pull](#pull-an-agent) the latest or a pinned commit at runtime to inject context into your agent, and use additional methods to [check existence](#check-whether-a-repo-exists), [list and search](#list-agents-and-skills) repos, and [delete](#delete-an-agent-or-skill) what you no longer need.

pages.title: observability
pages.description: LangSmith Observability provides full visibility into your LLM application: from individual traces to production-wide performance metrics. Traces are the record of what your agents did in production. Use them to debug failures, monitor quality, and build the datasets you evaluate against.

pages.title: observability-concepts
pages.description: LangSmith Observability lets you record, inspect, and analyze every step your AI agent takes. This page explains how that data is structured and visualized in LangSmith as well as how to start sending traces.

pages.title: observability-llm-tutorial
pages.description: In this tutorial, you will build a customer support chatbot using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and add LangSmith observability at each stage of development, from early prototyping through production.

pages.title: observability-quickstart
pages.description: LangSmith gives you end-to-end visibility into your agent by capturing [*traces*](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/observability-concepts.md#traces); a complete record of every step that ran during a request, from the inputs passed in to the final output returned.

pages.title: observability-stack
pages.description: LangSmith applications expose telemetry data that can be sent to the backend of your choice. If you don’t already have an observability stack, or prefer to keep LangSmith telemetry separate from your main application, you can use the LangSmith Observability Helm chart to deploy a basic observability stack.

pages.title: observability-studio
pages.description: LangSmith [Studio](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/studio.md) provides tools to inspect, debug, and improve your app beyond execution. By working with traces, datasets, and prompts, you can see how your application behaves in detail, measure its performance, and refine its outputs:

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-agent-definition
pages.description: The agent definition selects the model and core capabilities of a managed deep agent.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-agent-owned-interrupts
pages.description: An agent-owned interrupt is a pause that your own code creates. A tool posts a Slack message or modal that you design in [Block Kit](https://api.slack.com/block-kit), then calls `interrupt()`. When the user presses a button or submits the modal, Managed Deep Agents delivers the answer to the deployment as a `user_prompt_response` channel event and resumes the paused run with it. You can ask a user for structured input mid-run, such as an approval, a choice, or a set of form fields, without building a Slack app or a webhook of your own.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-browser-use
pages.description: Give a managed deep agent a browser to act on websites without a public API, such as booking a restaurant reservation, research a topic by following links across sites, or test an app through its UI after changing its code. The agent can navigate, click, fill forms, and inspect the result. Managed Deep Agents manages the browser and its tools.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-channels
pages.description: A channel makes a managed deep agent available in an external messaging service. Messages from the service can start agent runs, and the agent's final responses return through the same service.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-channels-http
pages.description: An HTTP channel turns a managed deep agent into an HTTP endpoint that any external service can call. Use it for a provider that Managed Deep Agents does not support directly, such as an order system, a support tool, or your own application.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-channels-slack
pages.description: A Slack channel lets people invoke a managed deep agent through app mentions, direct messages, and replies in an active Slack thread. Managed Deep Agents verifies Slack events, maps each conversation to a thread, runs the agent as the resolved caller, and posts the response back to Slack.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-cli
pages.description: The `mda` CLI compiles and deploys code-first [Managed Deep Agents](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-overview.md).

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-connections
pages.description: A connection links a managed deep agent to an external service such as GitHub, Notion, or Tavily. The credential lives in your LangSmith workspace. Use `connections.get(...)` in an authored tool or MCP server definition to resolve it at runtime.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-context-hub
pages.description: Managed Deep Agents stores deploy-owned instructions and skills, and optional durable memory, in [LangSmith Context Hub](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/use-the-context-hub.md). That split lets you change agent behavior without rebuilding application code, while the project remains the source of truth for lasting instruction and skill updates.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-custom-frontend
pages.description: A custom frontend is any application you write that calls a deployment directly instead of reaching the agent through a [channel](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-channels.md) or [LangSmith Studio](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-local-development.md#start-local-studio). Use one when the agent belongs inside a product surface you control, such as a support console, an internal dashboard, or a customer-facing chat page.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-deploy
pages.description: Deploying a Managed Deep Agent compiles a code-first project into a managed LangGraph app, syncs deploy-owned context to [Context Hub](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-context-hub.md), uploads the compiled source, and triggers a LangSmith hosted deployment build. The result is an [Agent Server](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/agent-server-overview.md) deployment, including the Agent Server API and [MCP endpoint](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-mcp-endpoint.md).

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-evals
pages.description: Managed Deep Agents evals are [Harbor](https://www.harborframework.com/docs/tasks) tasks. Use a coding agent with the [`eval-engineering` skill](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-skills/blob/main/config/skills/eval-engineering/SKILL.md) to inspect the project, draft a Task Spec for your review, and write complete tasks under `evals/`.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-identity
pages.description: Identity controls who can invoke your managed deep agent, such as apps and SDK clients that start runs or send messages.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-instructions
pages.description: Instructions define always-on agent behavior. They form the core of the agent's system prompt.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-local-development
pages.description: Install the project dependencies and add the model provider credentials to `.env`.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-mcp-connectors
pages.description: Connect a managed deep agent to remote [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/mcp.md) servers to add their tools to the agent. Managed Deep Agents creates the MCP client and loads the tools.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-mcp-endpoint
pages.description: Managed Deep Agents deployments run on [LangSmith Agent Server](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/agent-server-overview.md), so every deployment serves the Agent Server [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) (MCP) endpoint at `/mcp`. Any MCP client that supports the Streamable HTTP transport can call the deployed agent as a tool, so another assistant or agent can delegate work to it without calling the deployment API directly.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-memory
pages.description: Normally, a managed deep agent's conversational memory is scoped to a thread or session. Durable memory is optional knowledge that an agent can retain across threads, sessions, and deployments. Managed Deep Agents do not have durable memory by default.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-middleware
pages.description: Middleware adds behavior around model calls, tool calls, and the agent lifecycle. Like [custom tools](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-tools.md), MDA does not discover middleware automatically. Import it and pass it to the agent definition.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-migrate
pages.description: Managed Deep Agents runs the same [Deep Agents](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview.md) harness you already build against, so moving an existing agent is a repackaging job rather than a rewrite. Your tools, middleware, and subagents carry over as they are. The agent entry changes, and the system prompt, skills, and memory move into project files.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-overview
pages.description: Managed Deep Agents (MDA) is the simplest way to build and deploy production agents. You focus on what your agent does. MDA runs it. There are no servers to run and no infrastructure to wire together.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-project-structure
pages.description: A Managed Deep Agents project is a normal Python package with one required root agent entry. Other paths are either ordinary modules you import, or files and directories that MDA discovers to enable managed capabilities.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-quickstart
pages.description: Create and deploy your first Managed Deep Agent: scaffold a project, configure the model and instructions, add search, test in [LangSmith Studio](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/studio.md), and deploy with the [`mda` CLI](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-cli). Managed Deep Agents supplies the [Deep Agents harness](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview.md) and hosted runtime.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-runtime
pages.description: Agent factories, tools, and middleware hooks each receive a runtime. It is the native LangChain or LangGraph runtime with three managed fields added. Context, state, and the store work as they do in [LangChain](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/runtime.md), and your type checker sees your own context type.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-sandboxes
pages.description: A sandbox gives a managed deep agent an isolated filesystem and shell for working with files, running code, and executing commands.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-schedules
pages.description: Managed Deep Agents can run agents on a cron schedule. When you deploy the project, `mda deploy` provisions each schedule as a LangSmith cron after the deployment is live.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-search
pages.description: LangSmith manages the search infrastructure, so you can add search without hosting a service or creating a separate Parallel account or API key. The integration offers zero data retention.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-skills
pages.description: Skills package task-specific procedures and supporting files into reusable directories. MDA discovers them automatically. The agent loads a skill's full contents only when the task matches the description in the frontmatter.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-subagents
pages.description: Give a managed deep agent subagents to delegate specialized or context-heavy work, such as researching a topic, reviewing a change, or running a long task in the background with an async subagent while the agent keeps talking to the user. Each subagent has its own prompt and context window. It can also use its own model and tools.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-tools
pages.description: Custom tools are application code the agent can call for fetching real-time data, querying databases, executing code, and taking actions. Unlike [instructions](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-instructions.md) and [skills](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-skills.md), MDA does not discover them automatically.

pages.title: managed-deep-agents-tutorial
pages.description: This tutorial continues from the [quickstart](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/python/managed-deep-agents-quickstart.md). Use the `research-assistant` project you created there, with your model, instructions, and a working `mda dev` setup.

pages.title: studio
pages.description: Studio is a specialized agent IDE that enables visualization, interaction, and debugging of agentic systems that implement the Agent Server API protocol. Studio also integrates with [tracing](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/observability-concepts.md), [evaluation](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation.md), and [prompt engineering](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/prompt-context-hub.md#prompts).

pages.title: trace-claude-agent-sdk
pages.description: The [Claude Agent SDK](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) is an SDK for building agents with Claude. LangSmith provides native integration with the Claude Agent SDK to automatically trace your agent executions, tool calls, and interactions with Claude models.

pages.title: trace-claude-code
pages.description: The LangSmith tracing plugin sends your [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) conversations to LangSmith so you can see what the agent did. Each message becomes a trace, and a session's messages are grouped into a thread.

pages.title: trace-deep-agents
pages.description: This guide shows you how to enable LangSmith tracing for Deep Agents, view traces in the LangSmith UI, and (optionally) customize trace configuration for more advanced use cases.

pages.title: trace-with-codex
pages.description: The LangSmith tracing plugin sends your [OpenAI Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex) sessions to LangSmith so you can see what the agent did. Each turn becomes a trace, and a session's turns are grouped into a thread.

pages.title: trace-with-langchain
pages.description: LangSmith integrates seamlessly with LangChain (Python and JavaScript), the popular open-source framework for building agents.

pages.title: trace-with-langgraph
pages.description: LangSmith smoothly integrates with LangGraph (Python and JS) to help you trace agents, whether you're using LangChain modules or other SDKs.

pages.title: trace-with-opencode
pages.description: The `@langchain/langsmith-opencode` plugin sends [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) session traces to LangSmith. Use it to inspect agent turns, model metadata, token usage, tool calls, tool errors, attachments, and subagent activity from your OpenCode workflows.

pages.title: use-the-context-hub
pages.description: The **Context Hub** gives your team version-controlled, environment-aware management of the instructions and tools your agents use in production. A *context* is a versioned bundle of agent instructions and tools, either a skill or a full agent, that you manage in LangSmith.

pages.title: approval-modes
pages.description: By default, Deep Agents Code asks for your approval before running potentially consequential actions. These are called **gated actions** and include things like:

pages.title: cli-reference
pages.description: Deep Agents Code (`dcode`) accepts command-line flags at launch and exposes management subcommands for tools, agents, sessions, skills, credentials, and configuration. Use this page as a reference when you need to override defaults from the shell, run non-interactive tasks in scripts, or automate administration without opening a session. For installation and daily interactive use, see [Quickstart](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/quickstart.md). For how CLI flags fit into the broader configuration model, see [Configuration](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration).

pages.title: config-file
pages.description: default = "ollama:qwen3:4b"             # your intentional long-term preference

pages.title: configuration
pages.description: Deep Agents Code stores user configuration in its profile directory, which defaults to `~/.deepagents/`, and in project-level dotfiles. Administrators can enforce settings from a fixed system path with [`managed_config.toml`](#managed-configuration). For the full directory tree, session storage, and skill paths, see [Data locations](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration#data-locations).

pages.title: credentials
pages.description: Deep Agents Code needs an API key for each model provider you use. The recommended way to add one is the [`/auth`](#use-%2Fauth-recommended) credential manager. For non-interactive runs, manage the same stored keys from the shell with [`dcode auth`](#manage-credentials-from-the-shell-dcode-auth) or set [environment variables](#environment-variables-ci-and-headless) instead.

pages.title: extensions
pages.description: Python extensions customize the dcode agent server without modifying dcode itself. Use them to register model tools, LangChain middleware, virtual storage routes.

pages.title: goals-and-rubrics
pages.description: Goals and rubrics help Deep Agents Code check whether its work satisfies the criteria you care about. Use a goal for objective-driven work where the agent should help define acceptance criteria, and use a rubric when you already know the criteria.

pages.title: hooks
pages.description: Hooks let external programs observe and control Deep Agents Code lifecycle events.

pages.title: mcp-tools
pages.description: Add MCP servers by adding a `.mcp.json` config file to your project for project-level scope, or at user-level to apply to all projects.

pages.title: memory-and-skills
pages.description: There are two primary ways to customize an agent in Deep Agents Code:

pages.title: overview
pages.description: Deep Agents Code (`dcode`) is an open source coding agent built on the [Deep Agents SDK](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/quickstart.md).

pages.title: plugins
pages.description: Plugins extend dcode with reusable [skills](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/memory-and-skills.md), [MCP servers](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/mcp-tools.md), [hooks](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/hooks.md), and [Python extensions](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/extensions.md). Marketplaces provide catalogs for discovering and installing plugins across projects or teams. dcode supports Claude- and Codex-style plugin manifests and marketplace catalogs, as described in [Create a plugin](#create-a-plugin) and [Create a marketplace](#create-a-marketplace).

pages.title: providers
pages.description: Deep Agents Code supports any [chat model provider compatible with LangChain](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/chat.md), unlocking use for virtually any LLM that supports tool calling. Any service that exposes an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible API also works out of the box—see [Compatible APIs](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/config-file.md#compatible-apis).

pages.title: quickstart
pages.description: Deep Agents Code (`dcode`) is a terminal coding agent built on the [Deep Agents SDK](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/quickstart.md). This guide covers installation, your first task, daily interactive use, automation with piping, and LangSmith tracing. For a feature overview, see [Deep Agents Code overview](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/overview.md). For `config.toml` and provider settings, see [Configuration](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/deepagents/code/configuration).

pages.title: remote-sandboxes
pages.description: Deep Agents Code uses the [sandbox as tool](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/sandboxes.md#sandbox-as-tool-pattern) pattern: the `dcode` process (LLM loop, memory, tool dispatch) runs on your machine, but agent tool calls (`read_file`, `write_file`, `execute`, etc.) target the remote sandbox, not your local filesystem. To get files into the sandbox, use a [setup script](#setup-scripts) or the provider's file transfer APIs (see [Working with files](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/sandboxes.md#working-with-files)).

pages.title: subagents
pages.description: Define custom synchronous [subagents](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/subagents.md) as markdown files so Deep Agents Code can delegate specialized tasks to them.

pages.title: automate-updates
pages.description: OpenWiki can refresh repository documentation on a schedule and open a pull request or merge request when the wiki changes. Example workflows ship in the [OpenWiki repository](https://github.com/langchain-ai/openwiki/tree/main/examples).

pages.title: cli-reference
pages.description: OpenWiki ships as a single `openwiki` binary for interactive chat and one-shot documentation runs. For installation and first use, see [Quickstart](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/quickstart.md).

pages.title: code-mode
pages.description: Code mode builds a repository wiki in `openwiki/` with durable details such as architecture, integrations, and workflows. Coding agents use that wiki as context so they can work in the package more efficiently, with less rediscovery and fewer tokens. Humans can read the same Markdown, but agents are the primary audience. Agents discover the wiki through the pointer OpenWiki maintains in `AGENTS.md`, and through an `@AGENTS.md` import in `CLAUDE.md` when that file already exists.

pages.title: customize
pages.description: Customize OpenWiki with ignore rules, wiki briefs, agent instruction pointers, and telemetry.

pages.title: integrations
pages.description: OpenWiki can run inside an existing coding agent instead of launching its own model. The coding agent investigates the repository, plans the wiki, and writes each assigned page with its native repository tools. OpenWiki owns the durable page-job lifecycle, Claims validation and persistence, source-drift handling, and deterministic finalization.

pages.title: overview
pages.description: OpenWiki is an open source CLI that writes and maintains a Markdown wiki about your codebase or personal knowledge. The wiki captures details such as architecture, integrations, evals, and workflows so [coding agents](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview.md) can use it as durable context instead of rediscovering the repository on every task.

pages.title: personal-mode
pages.description: Personal mode builds a local personal brain wiki in `~/.openwiki/wiki` from configured sources such as local repositories, Custom MCP, Gmail, Notion, web search, Hacker News, Slack, and X/Twitter.

pages.title: providers
pages.description: OpenWiki supports the following providers:

pages.title: quickstart
pages.description: OpenWiki is a CLI that writes and maintains a Markdown wiki for your codebase or personal knowledge. Coding agents use that wiki as durable context, so they spend less time and fewer tokens rediscovering architecture, integrations, and other repository details. Humans can read the same docs, but agents are the primary audience. This guide covers installation, provider setup, and your first documentation run. For a feature overview, see [OpenWiki overview](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/openwiki/overview.md).

pages.title: search-and-link
pages.description: OpenWiki exposes local, read-only retrieval tools so coding agents can answer concrete questions from an existing wiki without starting a generation run. Use `openwiki link` to group related repository wikis into a named workspace, then search and read across that workspace.

pages.title: visualize

pages.title: custom-workflow
pages.description: In the **custom workflow** architecture, you define your own bespoke execution flow using [LangGraph](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview.md). You have complete control over the graph structure—including sequential steps, conditional branches, loops, and parallel execution.

pages.title: handoffs
pages.description: In the **handoffs** architecture, behavior changes dynamically based on state. The core mechanism: [tools](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/tools.md) update a state variable (e.g., `current_step` or `active_agent`) that persists across turns, and the system reads this variable to adjust behavior—either applying different configuration (system prompt, tools) or routing to a different [agent](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/agents.md). This pattern supports both handoffs between distinct agents and dynamic configuration changes within a single agent.

pages.title: handoffs-customer-support
pages.description: The [state machine pattern](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/multi-agent/handoffs.md) describes workflows where an agent's behavior changes as it moves through different states of a task. This tutorial shows how to implement a state machine by using tool calls to dynamically change a single agent's configuration—updating its available tools and instructions based on the current state. The state can be determined from multiple sources: the agent's past actions (tool calls), external state (such as API call results), or even initial user input (for example, by running a classifier to determine user intent).

pages.title: Multi-agent
pages.description: Multi-agent systems coordinate specialized components to tackle complex workflows. However, not every complex task requires this approach—a single agent with the right (sometimes dynamic) tools and prompt can often achieve similar results.

pages.title: router
pages.description: In the **router** architecture, a routing step classifies input and directs it to specialized [agents](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/agents.md). This is useful when you have distinct **verticals** (separate knowledge domains that each require their own agent).

pages.title: router-knowledge-base
pages.description: The **router pattern** is a [multi-agent](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/multi-agent.md) architecture where a routing step classifies input and directs it to specialized agents, with results synthesized into a combined response. This pattern excels when your organization's knowledge lives across distinct **verticals** (separate knowledge domains that each require their own agent with specialized tools and prompts).

pages.title: skills
pages.description: In the **skills** architecture, specialized capabilities are packaged as invocable "skills" that augment an [agent's](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/agents.md) behavior. Skills are primarily prompt-driven specializations that an agent can invoke on-demand.

pages.title: skills-sql-assistant
pages.description: This tutorial shows how to use **progressive disclosure** - a context management technique where the agent loads information on-demand rather than upfront - to implement **skills** (specialized prompt-based instructions). The agent loads skills via tool calls, rather than dynamically changing the system prompt, discovering and loading only the skills it needs for each task.

pages.title: subagents
pages.description: In the **subagents** architecture, a central main [agent](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/agents.md) (often referred to as a **supervisor**) coordinates subagents by calling them as [tools](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/tools.md). The main agent decides which subagent to invoke, what input to provide, and how to combine results. By default, subagents are stateless—they don't remember past interactions, with all conversation memory maintained by the main agent. This provides [context](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/context-engineering.md) isolation: each subagent invocation works in a clean context window, preventing context bloat in the main conversation.

pages.title: subagents-personal-assistant
pages.description: The **supervisor pattern** is a [multi-agent](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/multi-agent.md) architecture where a central supervisor agent coordinates specialized worker agents. This approach excels when tasks require different types of expertise. Rather than building one agent that manages tool selection across domains, you create focused specialists coordinated by a supervisor who understands the overall workflow.

pages.title: test
pages.description: Agentic applications let an LLM decide its own next steps to solve a problem. That flexibility is powerful, but the model's black-box nature makes it hard to predict how a tweak in one part of your agent will affect the whole. To build production-ready agents, thorough testing is essential.

pages.title: evals
pages.description: Evaluations ("evals") measure how well your agent performs by assessing its execution trajectory, the sequence of messages and tool calls it produces. Unlike [integration tests](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/test/integration-testing.md) that verify basic correctness, evals score agent behavior against a reference or rubric, making them useful for catching regressions when you change prompts, tools, or models.

pages.title: integration-testing

Unlike [unit tests](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/test/unit-testing.md) that use fakes and mocks, integration tests make actual network calls to confirm that components work together, credentials are valid, and latency is acceptable.

pages.title: unit-testing
pages.description: Unit tests exercise small, deterministic pieces of your agent in isolation. By replacing the real LLM with an in-memory fake (AKA fixture), you can script exact responses (text, tool calls, and errors) so tests are fast, free, and repeatable without API keys.

pages.title: tools

Because LangGraph runs the latest deployed graph against state that has been [persisted](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/persistence.md) for existing threads, every change you ship is effectively a backward-compatible API change with respect to your existing checkpoints.

pages.title: overview
pages.description: Trusted by companies shaping the future of agents—including Klarna, Uber, J.P. Morgan, and more—LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework and runtime for building, managing, and deploying long-running, stateful agents. LangGraph gives you fine-grained control to mix deterministic, hand-coded steps with LLM-driven agentic steps in the same graph, so you can build bespoke agents that behave exactly the way your application requires.
